headline: French Blood Service Finds Temperature Changes at Three Sites
deck: EFS says cold-room controls changed through a provider’s solution; its alarms detected the anomalies before blood products or samples were altered.
body: The French Blood Establishment said a cybersecurity incident produced anomalies in cold rooms equipped with a provider’s solution, changing their operating parameters and setting temperature and defrost thresholds to very high levels. [E1]
Cold storage rooms at three French Blood Establishment sites were affected on Monday, with temperature and defrosting thresholds massively increased, The Verge reported. [E2]
EFS said no health impacts had been identified and no losses of blood products had been reported. [E6]

The blood-service disruption followed refrigeration problems at supermarkets in Belgium, Estonia, Finland, Ireland, Italy, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Portugal and Sweden, AFP reported on 3 November. [E7]
EFS said its monitoring and alarm systems quickly identified the anomalies and enabled measures to ensure no samples or blood products were altered. [E3]
Its technical teams are working with the French National Cybersecurity Agency and the Health Ministry, EFS said. [E4]
EFS said it had stepped up monitoring of the operation and temperatures of all its equipment. [E5]

evidence_box.fragment: Although the EFS was not directly targeted by this cybersecurity incident, anomalies were reported, resulting in changes to the operating parameters of cold rooms equipped with the provider’s solution. Specifically, temperature and defrost thresholds were set to very high temperatures.
